summary: Scheduled Sunday check: the relevant arXiv new-listing pages still pointed to the Friday, 31 July 2026 batch, so no newly posted qualifying heavy-ion or physics-AI/ML papers were identified in the strict Sunday window. The latest scientifically relevant screened items remain STAR hypernuclei production in RHIC isobars, a physics-informed CGC nuclear dipole extraction, and cautiously useful AI/ML workflow or benchmark papers for heavy-ion and HEP transfer.
strongest_paper: No newly posted qualifying paper in the August 2 Sunday check; see 2026-07-31 for the latest full selection.
top_takeaway: No fresh Sunday arXiv batch was available. The latest valid selection remains the July 31 report, led by STAR hypernuclei production and the physics-informed CGC dipole-amplitude extraction.

carried_forward_highlights.title: Probing (Hyper)Nuclei Wave Functions and Production Mechanisms in sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV Isobar Collisions at RHIC
carried_forward_highlights.abstract: STAR reports centrality-dependent hypernuclei and light-nuclei production in 200 GeV Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions, with ratios favoring realistic non-Gaussian coalescence wave functions over simple thermal expectations.

carried_forward_highlights.title: Unbiased Data-Driven Determination of the Nuclear Dipole Amplitude in the Color Glass Condensate
carried_forward_highlights.authors_short: Si-Wei Dai, Haowu Duan, Long-Gang Pang, Guang-You Qin, Shu-Yi Wei, Han-Zhong Zhang, Wenbin Zhao
carried_forward_highlights.abstract: The paper embeds collinearly improved BK evolution and positivity constraints into a neural extraction of the Pb dipole amplitude from forward-hadron and coherent J/psi photoproduction data.

carried_forward_highlights.title: Relativistic transport near moving interfaces
carried_forward_highlights.abstract: A formal treatment of linear disturbances near moving planar interfaces in relativistic media, unifying boundary layers, wakes, and shock-tail asymptotics through a propagator and mode-selection construction.

carried_forward_highlights.title: CLVisc Agent for autonomous relativistic hydrodynamics studies
carried_forward_highlights.authors_short: Qi Wang, Long-Gang Pang, Shi Pu, Xin-Nian Wang
carried_forward_highlights.abstract: The paper demonstrates an LLM-agent workflow that learns CLVisc operations, runs 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic simulations, performs scans, compares results, and generates figures for eta/s and O+O nuclear-structure case studies.

carried_forward_highlights.title: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Collider Physics with Multi-Domain Adaptation
carried_forward_highlights.authors_short: Liangyu Wu, Qibin Liu, Alexander Yue, Julia Gonski
carried_forward_highlights.abstract: NEXUS pretrains a small autoencoder on charged-particle track features from collider data and fine-tunes for kinematic regression and event classification with limited labels.

carried_forward_highlights.title: DoTime: A Synthetic Benchmark Generator for Interventional and Counterfactual Time Series
carried_forward_highlights.authors_short: Dennis Thumm, Billy Tim Anthony, Ying Chen
carried_forward_highlights.abstract: DoTime creates temporal structural causal model benchmarks with interventions, counterfactuals, regime switches, nonstationarity, and exact ground truth for evaluating causal time-series models.

cautions.title: Photon-calibrated event-activity bias and subcollision geometry in d+Au collisions at sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV with PYTHIA 8 Angantyr
cautions.authors_short: Muhammad Ajaz, Haifa I. Alrebdi, Muhammad Waqas
cautions.abstract: A PYTHIA 8 Angantyr generator-level study of hard-event activity bias in d+Au collisions using photons, pions, and jets. The abstract notes that the calculation does not identify a unique microscopic origin for residual correlations.
